item.title: EAM Jaishankar will hold talks with Marco Rubio in Mumbai on Oct 20: MEA
item.description: The discussions are expected to cover key areas of bilateral cooperation, including energy, critical energy issues, and regional and global developments, the MEA said ...
item.dc:creator: Akshita Singh
item.content:encoded: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar will hold talks with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Mumbai on October 20, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said on Friday. Rubio is also expected to meet with Reliance Industries Ltd (RIL) Chairman Mukesh Ambani in Jamnagar, Gujarat, during his India trip. On Thursday, US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor said Rubio would travel to Jamnagar, home to RIL's oil refining complex, the world's largest, where he will meet Reliance officials. “I’d imagine he’d be there,” Gor said, referring to Ambani, at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi.Jaishankar-Rubio talks to focus on bilateral tiesAt the MEA's bi-weekly media briefing, spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said Jaishankar will host the UAE's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister in Mumbai on October 19 and 20. On October 20, he will hold talks with Rubio and attend celebrations marking the 250th anniversary of the United States as the guest of honour. “The meeting would be an opportunity to review the US-India relations and discuss ways to further strengthen our cooperation and global strategic partnership. It will also allow both sides to advance our shared priorities,” Jaiswal said. The discussions are expected to cover key areas of bilateral cooperation, including energy, critical energy issues, and regional and global developments, he added. The US State Department said earlier this week that Rubio would meet senior Indian government officials during his October 17-22 visit. The discussions are expected to focus on enhanced energy cooperation and strengthening the partnership between the two countries.MEA explains choice of Mumbai for meetingAsked why the meeting would take place in Mumbai rather than New Delhi, Jaiswal said India had hosted foreign dignitaries outside the national capital on several occasions over the past decade. He cited the Prime Minister's meetings with the Spanish Prime Minister in Vadodara, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz in Ahmedabad and the Prime Minister of Mauritius in Varanasi. He also referred to the SCO Foreign Ministers' Summit in Goa, hosted by Jaishankar, and the Heart of Asia conference in Amritsar.

item.title: RBI approves amalgamation of Emirates NBD's Indian branches with RBL Bank
item.description: The amalgamation will take effect on December 1, 2026, following Emirates NBD's acquisition of a 60 per cent stake in RBL Bank through a Rs 26,000 crore capital infusion ...
item.dc:creator: Our Bureau
item.content:encoded: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Friday approved the Scheme of Amalgamation of the Indian branches of Emirates NBD Bank P.J.S.C. with RBL Bank Limited, effective December 1, 2026. In June 2026, Emirates NBD completed the acquisition of a majority stake in RBL Bank through a primary capital infusion of about Rs 26,000 crore. Emirates NBD now holds 60 per cent of the expanded share capital of RBL Bank. The board has approved the appointment of five nominee directors of Emirates NBD as additional non-executive, non-independent directors on the bank's board, effective June 18, 2026, subject to shareholder approval. The transaction, which was first announced in October 2025, was completed after receiving all regulatory approvals and satisfying closing conditions. The deal constitutes the largest foreign direct investment in the Indian banking sector.

item.title: Iveco Group shareholders approve Tata Motors' takeover proposals
item.description: Iveco shareholders approve takeover-related resolutions, lowering the minimum acceptance threshold to 80 per cent; Tata Motors' €3.91 billion tender offer is set to close on October 26 ...
item.dc:creator: Sohini Das
item.content:encoded: Iveco Group on Friday approved all resolutions related to Tata Motors’ proposed acquisition of the Italian commercial vehicle manufacturer, clearing a key hurdle for the transaction and reducing the minimum share acceptance threshold from 95 per cent to 80 per cent. The resolutions were approved at an extraordinary general meeting (EGM) held in Amsterdam, Iveco said in a statement. The approval fulfils several conditions required for Tata Motors’ acquisition vehicle to declare its voluntary public tender offer unconditional, although the transaction remains subject to other conditions. Tata Motors, through its subsidiary TML CV Holdings, is seeking to acquire Iveco’s commercial vehicle business. The Indian automaker had on October 9 raised its offer price from €14.10 to €14.40 per share, valuing the transaction at approximately €3.91 billion. The reduction in the minimum acceptance threshold to 80 per cent is significant as it lowers the proportion of shares Tata Motors must secure to proceed with the acquisition, potentially easing the completion of the transaction. Shareholders also approved amendments to Iveco’s Articles of Association (AoA), its conversion from a publicly listed company into a private limited liability company following delisting, and the appointment of new board members effective upon settlement.The resolutions additionally provide for a post-offer demerger, which the acquirer may implement if it secures at least 80 per cent of Iveco’s common shares. Shareholders also authorised a subsequent share sale and potential dissolution of the existing corporate entity as part of the post-acquisition restructuring. The EGM further approved changes to Iveco’s special voting share arrangements, including termination of its loyalty voting structure following settlement. The acquisition is expected to strengthen Tata Motors’ position in the global commercial vehicle market by expanding its geographical presence and product portfolio, particularly in Europe. The tender offer is scheduled to close on October 26, unless extended. Completion will depend on the remaining offer conditions being satisfied.

item.title: Growth moderation, valuation headwinds ahead for Nestle despite strong Q2
item.description: Nestle posted 20% revenue growth and improved margins in Q2FY27, but concerns over slowing growth, input costs and premium valuations have prompted brokerages to cut target multiples ...
item.dc:creator: Ram Prasad Sahu
item.content:encoded:
Home / Markets / Stock Market News / Growth moderation, valuation headwinds ahead for Nestle despite strong Q2

Growth moderation, valuation headwinds ahead for Nestle despite strong Q2 Nestle posted 20% revenue growth and improved margins in Q2FY27, but concerns over slowing growth, input costs and premium valuations have prompted brokerages to cut target multiples premium

Nestlé India shares fall 8.6% in two sessions despite strong Q2 growth as brokerages trim valuation multiples. (Photo: Reuters)

Ram Prasad Sahu New Delhi 4 min read Last Updated : Oct 16 2026 | 5:56 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Fast moving consumer goods (FMCG) major Nestle delivered robust September quarter numbers, aided by double-digit volume growth.

While revenue growth was broad based with contributions across categories, margins saw an expansion despite elevated input costs.

While Q2 performance was strong, the stock has come under selling pressure shedding 8.6 per cent to ₹1,265 in two trading sessions.

The weak investor sentiment is on account of a top line growth moderation in H2FY27, input cost inflation, going ahead, and sharp divergence in valuation of Nestle vis-a-vis peers.

Given these concerns, most brokerages have cut their price-to-earnings multiple for the stock.

Continuing its momentum on the sales growth front, the company registered a 20 per cent year-on-year (Y-o-Y) growth in the September quarter on a high base.

Sales trend in the last four quarters on a standalone basis has been robust with growth in the range of 19-25 per cent Y-o-Y.

The gains on the back of double-digit volume growth were aided by confectionary and beverages segments.

Domestic and exports segments saw a growth of 20-22 per cent.

The company continued to expand its rural distribution, which led to robust double-digit growth in general trade across town tiers while e-commerce growth was led by quick commerce (qcom). The qcom segment was aided by channel-specific assortment and better digital shelf execution.

Organised trade gained from improved in-store execution, consumer activations, shelf visibility and store expansion.

Nestle expanded internationally with the launch of Maggi Masala-e-Magic in Canada, and Nescafe Sunrise expanded to five West African markets.

Commenting on the strong show in Q2, JM Financial Research says that the company reported strong domestic revenue growth at over 20 per cent with a two-year annual growth of 15.5 per cent led by double-digit volume growth.

This is expected to be the best-in-class among food and beverages as well as staples players.

Despite higher advertising spends and input costs, the company posted an improvement in profitability.

Gross margins saw an expansion of 260 basis points (bps) Y-o-Y to 56.9 per cent and this was largely on account of price hikes.

The company expects coffee and wheat to stay range bound while sugar and edible oil have stabilised at elevated price levels.

Cocoa remained volatile led by weather-led crop concerns. Higher supplies should help lower milk prices which have gone up.

While commodity outlook remains volatile, Nestlé’s portfolio and pricing power makes it the best placed to navigate the challenge, says JM Financial Research.

Mehul Desai and Pooja Kubadia of the brokerage believe that festival demand trends and sustaining volume momentum, going ahead, would be the key.

While the brokerage likes Nestlé’s execution but given the broader sector de-rating, it is cutting target multiple to 58 times from the 65 times earlier. It has maintained an add rating with a revised target price of ₹1,450 (earlier ₹1,610).

Though the company has been investing in its brands and saw a 46 per cent increase in marketing spends, operating profit grew by 33.3 per cent.

Margins at the operating level improved 223 bps Y-o-Y to 23.1 per cent, led by savings in employee cost.

Mihir P Shah and Riya Patni of Nomura Research expect price hikes along with continued mix improvement supported by new launches in premium offerings, to enable the company maintain its margins.

The brokerage has a ‘buy’ rating on the stock with a target price of ₹1,535 but has reduced its earnings estimates and target multiple from 65 times to 56 times.

Though Nestle’s strong financial performance versus peers will continue, top line growth rate will start moderating from Q3FY27, says the brokerage.

After the recent share price corrections across FMCG companies, the gap in valuation for Nestle against peers has widened (55 times against 35 times for the sector).

Nuvama Research has kept its estimates unchanged and maintained a ‘buy’ rating.

However, factoring in the broader market and staples de-rating, analysts led by Abneesh Roy have cut multiples to 60 times (from 65 times), yielding a revised target price of ₹1,740 (from ₹1,815 earlier).
